title: Native finite-stage open tensor datum existence
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, schemes X and Z in universe u, and an open immersion j:X -> Z. Fix n in N. At the positive quotient stage n+1, with the actual StrictTower.moduleJ, modulePullback, native adjunction and finitePullSection of [def-coef-native-open-tensor-evaluation-data], there exists an ordinary/cochain datum of [def-sf-open-tensor-cochain-data], namely NativeOpenTensorPrimitives.FiniteOpenCochainsData l E j n of [def-coef-native-open-tensor-primitives]. No sequence-site datum or family over n is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, separating the sequence-site and finite coefficient constructions.

proof.text: Identify the native open sites, coefficient sheaves, and exact module adjunctions with their localized-site presentations. Restriction of sheafification of tensor gives the natural ordinary restriction comparison and its specified pure-section formula. The ordinary direct image is the right adjoint of the native restriction. Fix n and use the constant ring compactSupportSystemLevel l E n throughout; no product site or family of data is required.
Restriction preserves flat sheaves and flat-term K-flat complexes by the pullback preservation theorem, on both the sequence site and each finite site.

Use the unit transpose of the inverse restriction/tensor comparison as the inverse ordinary projection. The ringed-slice tensor formula and open-unit normalization prove it invertible; adjunction uniqueness proves ordinary naturality.

For this fixed finite coefficient ring, totalize the ordinary comparison over all a+b=k using extension preservation of coproducts. On each summand naturality for each differential proves the signed chain equation; ordinary naturality for arbitrary module maps gives chainNaturality. The n=0 case is the first positive quotient, and requires no exception.
